en: The Scripture of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Clad in Leaves.

[Posthumous title of the translator: Grand Master of the Household, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sui with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, conferred purple robes, posthumously granted the rank of Minister of Works, and titled Dajian (Great Mirror).

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
He proclaimed the sublime Dharma to the great assembly.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, and...
Kneeling with both knees upon the ground, he prostrated at the feet of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and addressed him, saying:
"O Noble One, you abide in the liberation of great compassion and the illusion-like samādhi."
It is able to eliminate all the suffering and afflictions of sentient beings and bestow upon them mundane and supramundane benefit and happiness.
Even if all sentient beings within the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system were to...
At the same time, there are various forms of suffering and the sufferings of the eight difficult conditions.
Whether one aspires for worldly or supramundane fruits of retribution,
if one can single-mindedly recite the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, [one shall be delivered].
At the appropriate time, without abandoning the vow of great compassion,
he immediately manifests various bodies in accordance with the types of beings,
able to fulfill all the supreme aspirations of sentient beings.
It can also protect and maintain the boundaries of the nation and deliver beings from suffering and hardship;
it can also gather, nurture, and increase auspiciousness;
and it can also prevent and stop the suffering of imprisonment.
It can also eliminate the poisons of sorcery and malevolent spirits, as well as all malignant diseases;
it can also restrain swords and staves on the battlefield,
and it can dispel the calamities of water and fire.
It can also eliminate the curses of sorcery and incantations,
and it can establish protection for the cardinal directions and the boundaries of the earth.
We pray only that the Noble One will take pity on all future sentient beings, including kings, men, and women.
If there are those who have pure faith in the Three Jewels and protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma,
ensuring that the royal lineage is inherited without interruption—
for their sake, I shall explain the ritual procedures, dhāraṇīs, and methods of empowerment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat,
prostrated at the feet of the Buddha,
circumambulated him three times to the right, and returned to his original place to sit.
Joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I pray only that the World-Honored One will compassionately empower me.
I possess a dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Patra-cīvara Avalokiteśvara."
It is able to eliminate all calamities for sentient beings:
epidemics, famine, bandits, and weapons;
as well as irregularities in water and drought, and the disorder of the lunar mansions and planets.
"It can also increase merit and cause the realm to be prosperous and the people to be peaceful and happy.
I now wish to speak; I pray that you will grant me your permission.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent! Speak as you intend."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
receiving the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, spoke this dhāraṇī: *Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo amitābha*...
Āḥ vākya-tathāgatāya rāhate | Vyākhyāna-buddhāya | Nama ārya-avalokiteśvarāya | Mṛte sattvāya ||
5. Obeisance to the Great Sattvas (Mahāsattvāya)! 6. Obeisance to the Great Caruṇiṇī (Mahācaruṇiṇī)!

Oṃ praṇaśavari hūṃ phaṭ. When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken this dhāraṇī, he uttered it with a half-sound at the three times.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if a good man or a good woman recites this dhāraṇī even once,"
By reciting it once, one protects oneself;
by reciting it twice, one protects one's companions;
by reciting it three times, one can protect an entire household.
If one recites it four times, it protects a single village;
if one recites it five times, it protects an entire kingdom.
If an epidemic spreads within the kingdom...
One should take a piece of white cotton cloth one and a half cubits wide and two cubits long.
First, have the painter observe purity and the precepts of fasting.
Then, mix a small amount of blue vitriol with cow dung.
Mix with fragrant resin;
do not use hide glue.
Select a day under the lunar mansion of Mṛgaśiras.
Paint an image of the Bodhisattva Parṇaśavarī Avalokiteśvara.
This image should take the form of a celestial maiden (devī),
wearing a jeweled crown upon her head, in which is the Buddha Amitāyus.
Her body is adorned with necklaces, bracelets, and armlets;
her form is encircled by a halo of blazing flames.
She has four arms: the first right hand is held at the heart, grasping an auspicious fruit (*śrīvatsa*).
The second right hand forms the mudrā of granting boons;
the first left hand holds a battle-axe,
and the second left hand holds a lasso.
Seated upon a lotus flower;
once the painted image is completed, it should be suspended from a pole and held by one person.
The person holding the staff should recite the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā* Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara without interruption;
the sound of the drum and the ringing of the bell should be struck with the *Kilikilivajra* King Mantra.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times before striking it. The mantra is:
Oṃ kīṃ hūṃ (with a short, weak tone). Furthermore, have two people recite praises.
One person recites the *Śrī-vardhana-stotra* (Praise of Auspicious Increase),
and one person recites the *Maṅgala-stotra* (Praise of Auspiciousness).
Let three or five disciples who understand the Dharma [perform these].
One person shall hold an incense burner and burn agalloch (an-si) incense.
This incense should be empowered one hundred and eight times with the heart-mantra of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, using leaves as the offering cloth.
Thereafter, take up the incense smoke and ensure it does not cease.
One person shall hold a *bhadraghaṭa* (auspicious jar) filled with scented water and into which branches of flowering and fruit-bearing trees have been inserted.
He ordered the person carrying the vase to walk ahead and lead the image.
Two men blew conch shells as they were ushered into the royal palace, where they performed one circumambulation.
He went out through the southern gate and returned from the east;
he entered again and circumambulated the wards and markets within the city once,
then went out through the southern gate of the city.
Outside the southern gate of the city, place a large water jar.
Within it, place various foods, drinks, mixed fruits, and parched grain.
The ācārya recites the mantra of the Tathāgata of Wondrous Physical Form seven times to empower it.
Thereafter, recite the Dharani of the Bodhisattva Parṇaśavarī seven times.
Within the phrases of the mantra,
invoke the name of the king and perform the empowerment.
"May there be no calamities within the King's realm.
Thereafter, by the side of the road in the wilderness,
he cast down the water jar, causing it to break.
He spoke thus: "O disease-inflicting spirits and others who roam within the realm of Yama,
may you accept and partake of this food and drink."
Returning by the same path,
he gave rise to a heart of great compassion for all sentient beings,
causing this realm to be free from all calamities and disasters.
Furthermore, for one who desires to seek long life and freedom from illness,
one should draw an image of the Bodhisattva Parṇaśavarī on cotton cloth, according to one's preference for its size.
Beneath the hands of the Wish-Fulfilling Bestower (Varada),
paint those men and women;
place their images within the maṇḍala.
Every day, one should circumambulate while making offerings of incense, flowers, and food, and make vows;
thus, one will always receive empowerment and have all one's wishes fulfilled.
Furthermore, there is another method: if a king, or his sons or daughters, are difficult to raise or nourish...
Some suffer short lifespans, are beset by illness, or find themselves unable to sleep or eat in peace;
all these arise from the conditions of past karma that produce unfavorable planetary configurations (*nakṣatra*).
Or, they may frequently be oppressed by the five planets encroaching upon their natal constellation.
If it causes the body to feel uneasy,
then at the place where one resides,
use ox-gall (gorocana), or paper, or plain silk.
The mantras of the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals were written on paper and affixed to the four walls;
first, they were placed upon the eastern wall.
The mantras of the four great yakṣa generals are to be inscribed,
beginning from the northeast corner.
As for the mantra of the first yakṣa general, it is as follows:
Oṃ nīlakaṭa ki hūṃ vauṣaṭ svāhā. The second yakṣa general’s mantra is:
Oṃ sunetra kaṭa ki hūṃ vauṣaṭ svāhā. The third yakṣa general’s mantra is: [Oṃ]... svāhā.
Oṃ buraṇakaṭa ṭki hūṃ traḥ svāhā. The mantra of the fourth yakṣa general is:
Oṃ kapi-la-kaṭa ṭki hūṃ traḥ svāhā. Next, on the southern wall:
Affix the mantras of the four great yakṣa generals.
The mantra of the first yakṣa general is:
Oṃ saṃghāṭe hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. The mantra of the second yakṣa general is:
Oṃ upasaṃghaṭṭaki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. This is the mantra of the third yakṣa general.
Oṃ saṃkaraṭṭaki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. This is the mantra of the fourth yakṣa general.
Oṃ dānadaṃṣṭri hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. Next, on the western wall, affix the mantras of the four great yakṣa generals.
The mantra of the first yakṣa general is:
Oṃ haritaki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. The mantra of the second yakṣa general is:
Oṃ hṛtikṣata kīṃ hūṃ svāhā. This is the mantra of the third yakṣa general.
Oṃ prabhuṭṭaka kīṃ hūṃ svāhā. This is the mantra of the fourth yakṣa general.
Oṃ kapilataṭi hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. Next, on the northern wall, affix the mantras of the four great yakṣa generals.
The mantra of the first yakṣa general is:
Oṃ dharaṇāṭaka hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. The mantra of the second yakṣa general is:
Oṃ dharaṇāṭaka hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the mantra of the third yakṣa general.
Oṃ uṇigapāṭaka hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the mantra of the fourth yakṣa general.
Oṃ visanuda ji hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. Next, in the northeast corner, the mantra for the installation of one great yakṣa general is as follows:
Oṃ pañcika ṭa ki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. Next, in the southeast corner, the mantra for one great yakṣa general is as follows:
Oṃ bhañja rañjanta kīṃ hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. Next, in the southwest corner, the mantra for one great yakṣa general is as follows:
Oṃ saptagirīṭa jīṃ hūṃ svāhā. Next, at the northwest corner, the mantra for one great yakṣa general is as follows:
Oṃ hama-vataṭa-ki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. Next, on the stone beneath the feet where they do not tread in the lower direction, carve the mantras of the four great yakṣa generals.
Place them beneath the ground in the four directions.
The mantra of the great yakṣa general of the eastern subterranean region is:
Oṃ bhumuṭaki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. The mantra of the great yakṣa general of the southern subterranean region is:
Oṃ subhumataḥ hūṃ raḥ svāhā. This is the mantra of the great yakṣa general of the western subterranean realm.
Oṃ karataḥ hūṃ raḥ svāhā. This is the mantra of the great yakṣa general of the northern subterranean realm.
Oṃ upakaraṭa ji hūṃ vauṣaṭ svāhā. Next, on each of the four corners above the *śālā*, affix a mantra of one great yakṣa general.
The mantra of the great yakṣa general atop the dwelling in the northeast corner is:
Oṃ suriyatāki hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. The mantra of the great yakṣa general atop the dwelling in the southeast corner is:
Oṃ agniṭa kīṃ hūṃ vaḥ svāhā. This is the mantra of the great yakṣa general Śikhin, located on the southwest corner.
Oṃ somataki hūṃ raḥ svāhā. This is the mantra of the great yakṣa general in the northwest corner, situated on the roof.
Having recited the mantra Oṃ vāyutaki hūṃ raḥ svāhā.
Regarding the positions of the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals,
smear a small altar for each one with incense;
upon each altar, burn incense and scatter various flowers.
Having offered food, drink, lamps, candles, and *argha* water with sincere devotion, I pray:
May the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals, together with their retinues,
each dwelling in their respective directions, protect and guard [the name] so that calamities, misfortunes, diseases, and untimely death may be eliminated.
One attains an increase in physical strength and wisdom;
one becomes majestic, dignified, and fully endowed with excellence;
one is easy to nourish and easy to raise, and possesses a long life span.
Having performed this empowerment,
the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals did not dare to transgress the instructions of all the Buddhas,
as well as those of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Day and night they shall be protected; sleeping in peace and waking in peace, they shall attain great majesty and power.
If there is a king who performs this rite, all calamities and diseases within his realm shall be extinguished.
The land will be peaceful and the people joyful.
Furthermore, according to the Dharma, one should paint the *jātaka* constellations and make offerings to them every month.
If one performs such a rite,
even malevolent constellations will be transformed into auspicious ones.
One should carve an image of the Bodhisattva Parṇaśavarī Avalokiteśvara out of white sandalwood.
Furthermore, one should write this mantra on birch bark and wear it together [with other items].
If one performs this rite, one should receive empowerment on a day when the lunar mansion Āśleṣā is in conjunction with the moon.
The consecration flask has its neck tied with a silk cloth and is filled with scented water;
within the water are placed the seven precious gems and five kinds of medicinal herbs.
That which is called Sahakāra and so forth; sahaneva; khaṇḍakāri.
Vṛhati, kirāta, as well as the five seeds,
various fragrances, and so forth.
Recite the Parṇaśavarī Avalokiteśvara Dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times to empower it;
use this for consecration to wash away all obstacles and difficulties.
Having performed the consecration,
take a clay bowl and fill it with various kinds of food and drink;
circumambulate the heads of those men and women three times.
He ordered one who was knowledgeable in the Dharma to carry it far away and throw it down to break it.
Then, having fashioned a cord,
he empowered it with the Parṇaśavarī mantra and tied it upon his head.
If one performs this rite,
all diseases of the body, malevolent spirits, demonic possession, sorcery,
and the oppressive influence of the planetary deities upon one's natal constellation shall be entirely extinguished.
Furthermore, there is another method:
if a person suffers from an epidemic, take *śamī* wood—or if that is unavailable in this country, substitute with mulberry (*kō*) wood—and kindle a fire.
Then, perform *homa* with clarified butter while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times, casting human hair and human bone into the fire to be burned.
Having made daily offerings for seven days to the Bodhisattva Parṇaśavarī Avalokiteśvara,
at the time of the homa ritual:
By reciting the names of that kingdom, the city, the district, and the village,
all calamities shall be entirely extinguished.
This includes such things as epidemics of elephants, epidemics of horses, epidemics of cattle, and epidemics of water buffaloes.
If one takes bone, wood, or hair from each of their respective species and performs *homa* for seven days and seven nights, all calamities will likewise be extinguished.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a jar and fill it completely with scented water.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times to empower water, with which you shall sprinkle that animal;
all pestilential diseases will be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, there is another method: if a person suffers from a headache.
Take fragrant flowers and empower them one hundred and eight times;
if one has them smelled by the nose, the affliction will be immediately cured.
Furthermore, there is another method for those afflicted by spirits.
Take powdered rice from a *mātrikā* (sorcery ritual) and carry it away to fashion the form of that *mātrikā*. Then,
using a sharp blade while reciting [the mantra], cut it into pieces segment by segment.
If one performs *homa* for seven days, one will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, there is another method: if a person suffers from malaria that recurs every day, every two days, or every three days.
Even for cases lasting up to seven days or for a long duration,
if one suffers from malaria, one should write this mantra with ox-gallstone (gorocana);
by wearing it, one will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, there is a method for infants afflicted by malevolent spirits:
if one writes this mantra and wears it, they shall be cured.
Furthermore, there is a method for when bandits invade and plunder market towns, villages, or districts.
If one wishes to travel afar and fears robbers or thieves, one should take powdered khadira wood and perform a homa while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Wherever one goes, there will be no obstacles or difficulties.
Furthermore, there is a method: if insects are eating the crops, take sand and empower it one hundred and eight times with the mantra.
Scatter it in the field, and the insects will depart of their own accord; the five grains will ripen in abundance.
